title: Advancing Chronic Pain Care in Rural Seniors: Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing to Improve Understanding, Assessment, and Comorbidity Risk Prediction
text:
With the intention to better understand the complex issue of chronic pain in rural older adults, this project
proposes two pivotal objectives: (1) improving the understanding and measurement of the pain experience
through advanced modeling technologies that incorporate varied dimensions of pain, and (2) developing
predictive models to identify individuals with chronic pain at risk for depression and cognitive
impairment. By integrating natural language processing, machine learning, and comprehensive data
analysis, the proposed research aims to develop tools to automate assessment of pain and identification of
individuals at risk for depression and cognitive concerns, capitalizing on existing medical record data for
immediate predictions. These tools can be particularly advantageous in rural settings where access to
physicians, especially specialists, is limited, offering medical care providers critical insights for prompt
intervention and ultimately improving the quality of life among this vulnerable population.

title: Modeling Enhancer Hijacking in Cancer via Genome Engineering and Single-Cell Sequencing
text:
Gene activation depends on the communication between the enhancer and the gene promoter. Transcription
factors are known to mediate and regulate this process through binding to the genomic DNA. This proposal
aims to investigate the role of transcription factors and genomic sequences in oncogene regulation, and further
model oncogene activation in human cancer.

title: Missense Variants in Myosin Binding Protein C that Cause Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
text:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common genetic heart condition that causes sudden
cardiac death and congestive heart failure, and for which current treatments do not slow or
prevent progression of the condition. The gene that is most commonly mutated in HCM is called
myosin binding protein C. The goals of this study are to understand how mutations in myosin
binding protein C affect how the protein associates with other binding partners, and whether
these effects can be reversed therapeutically by delivery of the normal protein using gene
therapy.

title: Moderators and Mediators of Within-Person Risk for Contact and Non-Contact Sexual Aggression in College Men
text:
Alcohol-related sexually aggressive behavior (SAB) by college men is a highly prevalent and serious problem
on college campuses in the US, and prevention programs targeting men have not produced a sustained
reduction in SAB. The current study will use an EMA burst design (4 bi-annual surveys with corresponding 28-
day daily assessments) to examine daily effects of within-person risk and protective factors for both non-
contact and contact SAB, and theoretically relevant moderators and mediators of these effects. Identifying
malleable risk and protective factors, characteristics of those most at risk, and mechanisms of effects of
alcohol use and drinking contexts on SAB may inform the development/refinement of both traditional
prevention/intervention programs and ecological momentary interventions targeting `in the moment' risk factors
for SAB.

title: Investigation into the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics, intra-organelle communication, and metabolic reprogramming by the PKA-fusion oncoprotein
text:
Fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC) is a rare and aggressive liver cancer affecting adolescents and young adults, with
no effective treatments for advanced disease. Our work using novel patient-derived models and engineered
systems expressing the DNAJB1-PRKACA fusion gene (PKAfus) has revealed that PKAfus disrupts mitochondrial
dynamics and lysosomal function, leading to metabolic rewiring that supports tumor progression. Therefore, this
study will elucidate the mechanisms by which PKAfus-driven organelle dysfunction fuels tumor growth and identify
metabolic vulnerabilities that can be therapeutically targeted, paving the way for new treatment strategies for
FLC and related tumors.

title: REmote symptom COllection to improVE postopeRative care (RECOVER)
text: This proposal aims to employ artificial intelligence (AI) and natural language processing (NLP) technologies and conduct a randomized clinical trial to examine how a voice-assisted, remote patient symptom monitoring system (VARSMS) can reduce ethnoracial disparities after gastrointestinal (GI) cancer surgery. Black and Hispanic patients experience more difficult social and medical conditions while recovering at home than White patients, which makes a home-based “smart” intervention potentially transformative. Further, our system would replace less flexible and adaptable telephone-based systems currently in use.

title: Clinical Validation of Metabolic Markers Detected by Mass Spectrometry Imaging for Diagnosis of Thyroid Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsies
text:
Diagnosis of a fine needle aspiration (FNA) biopsies obtained from patients with a suspicious thyroid nodules
can be extremely challenging using standard clinical pathology workflows. The majority of patients that receive
an indeterminate biopsy result undergo a diagnostic surgery to later find out that the surgical procedure was
completely unnecessary, leading to life-altering side effects. Here, we propose to conduct a large validation study
to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of a new molecular test we have developed to diagnose FNA
biopsies based on the detection of hundreds of metabolic markers, with the expectation to improve diagnosis
and thus reduce the number of unnecessary diagnostic thyroid surgeries for patients.

title: Long noncoding RNA regulation of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease
text:
Cardiovascular disease remains the number one cause of death in the United States. Emerging data indicate
important roles for non-coding RNAs in the regulation of inflammation and atherosclerosis, yet this is an
understudied area. Our work aims to fill this void by investigating how long noncoding RNAs contribute to
cardiovascular disease, with the ultimate goal of identifying novel diagnostic approaches and therapeutic targets
for its treatment.

title: Molecular determinants and consequences of disease-specific tau conformers in neurons and glia
text:
The singular objective of this COMBINE project is to understand how the cellular milieu shapes tau self-assembly
in Alzheimer's disease related disorders (ADRDs). To accomplish this goal, a diverse team of investigators will
leverage an integrated multidisciplinary approach in human brain samples, human IPSC-derived cell lines, and
rodent models of ADRD tauopathy. By elucidating the roots of this cell type-specific complexity, this research will
illuminate novel mechanisms and biomarkers of disease etiology and phenotypic diversity, thus providing new
directions for the development of more precise molecular diagnostics and tau conformer-specific therapeutics.

title: Elucidating the molecular mechanisms behind human neurodevelopmental disorders using brain organoids
text:
Brain organoids are emerging as powerful tools for studying the mechanisms behind human brain development
and disease. In our recent studies, we developed a platform for assembling functional neural circuits that
exhibit surprisingly complex neural network activities such as oscillatory rhythms. In the proposed studies, we
will explore how brain organoids can be best utilized to discover the mechanisms behind a range of
neurological disorders and develop strategies for therapeutic development.

title: Nano-CRISPR extracellular vesicle sensing system for longitudinal tumor monitoring
text:
The overall goal of this proposal is to further advance the cutting-edge plasmonic EV sensing technology for
multiplexed protein and RNA biomarker analysis in single EVs. Using longitudinal clinical samples collected
during therapy, we will assess the clinical utilities of EV analyses for monitoring and evaluating treatment
response in ovarian cancer.

title: Core C Admin Core
text: CORE C: ADMINISTRATIVE (Core Leader: Chris Sasse9) Abstract: The success of the Systems Genetics of Tuberculosis (SGTB) Program requires a robust scientific and programmatic infrastructure to ensure smooth coordination and implementation across program components and activities. As the hub of this program, the Administrative Core will continue to provide both scientific and administrative oversight to facilitate effective communication among projects and cores and to ensure that resources are used efficiently to achieve our common scientific goals. The Administrative Core will be directed by Program PD/PI Dr. Sassetti, who will be supported by an external Scientific Advisory Board. The Administrative Core will ensure fiscal oversight and regulatory compliance, facilitate communication, manage strategic planning, and oversee data and resources management and sharing.

title: Real-Time Motion Correction Method for a Portable, High-Resolution TOF PET Scanner for Imaging the Brain, Head, and Neck
text:
Head and neck cancer is a significant global health concern, and accurate detection of cervical lymph node
metastases is critical for effective staging and treatment. This research aims to develop a portable, high-
resolution time-of-flight PET imaging system with real-time motion correction to improve the detection of small
tumors and lymph node metastases in patients with head and neck cancer. By enhancing diagnostic accuracy
and reducing unnecessary surgeries, this technology has the potential to improve patient outcomes, advance
treatment planning, and expand access to high-quality imaging.

title: Mapping the B-Cell Repertoire Induced by HIV Vaccination: A Bioinformatics Platform for Integrated Analysis of B-Cell Receptor Sequences and Antibody Functions
text:
Making data from research studies publicly available is a cornerstone of open science. The massive, complex,
and protected B-cell receptor sequencing data and associated antibody structural and functional data generated
by phase 1 studies of candidate broadly neutralizing antibody-inducing HIV vaccines pose unique data sharing
challenges. This project will develop resources for publicly sharing these data, thus fostering innovation,
collaboration, and scientific advancement.

title: In Silico periodontal multiepitope vaccine through bioinformatics and immunoinformatics
text:
Periodontal disease affects more than 40% of the global adult population, which is not only a significant cause
of tooth loss but also a risk factor for many non-communicable diseases, including cardiovascular disease,
diabetes, lung disease, pregnancy complications, obesity, and cancer. The risk of tooth loss from periodontal
disease is compounded by compromised access to dental care in underrepresented populations that experience
health disparities. Developing an efficacious periodontal vaccine could directly address these public health
concerns, enhance the global population's quality of life, and help reduce the burden of comorbid conditions in
both general populations and those experiencing health disparities.

title: The Jackson Laboratory Center for Precision Genetics
text:
OVERALL
Although our understanding of the genetic causes of human disease continues to grow, the translation of these
discoveries into clinical application remains cumbersome and slow. The goal of the JAX Center for Precision
Genetics (JCPG) is to overcome these challenges through the development and preclinical deployment of
advanced mouse models of human disease, in support of the biomedical and rare disease communities. Our
goal is to transform the process and speed by which human disease discoveries are translated into treatments
for patients.

title: Investigating the role of noncoding RNAs in malaria parasites through targeted Cas13-mediated degradation
text:
Malaria is a severe infectious disease responsible for extensive morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan
Africa and many other regions of the developing world and is especially devasting to young children and
pregnant women. This project will establish a new method to manipulate gene expression in cultured
parasites as a tool to explore the mechanisms by which malaria parasites avoid the immune response of
infected individuals. A better understanding of these processes could enable new methods to control the
disease and address the significant impact malaria has on the developing world.

title: Development of a Dual-Action Oral Immunotherapy for Clostridioides difficile Prevention
text:
Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) causes a life-threatening disease. Currently there is no prevention. This
project advances a novel oral immunotherapy to prevent the infection and disease transmission, thus
addressing antimicrobial resistance and healthcare-associated infections.

title: Human and Translational Immunology Training Program
text:
HUMAN AND TRANSLATIONAL IMMUNOLOGY TRAINING PROGRAM (HTITP)
The Human and Translational Immunology Training Program (HTITP) trains scientists with expertise in
advancing translational immune research and therapies. HTITP trainees learn the most advanced techniques
and approaches available to excel and become the next leaders and innovators in translational research.

title: Network biomarkers for early detection of cognitive impairment using digital clock drawings
text:
Our research aims to transform the early detection of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias by developing
advanced AI tools using digital neuropsychological tests. By analyzing detailed data from these tests, we can
identify subtle cognitive impairments that were previously undetectable. This innovative approach aims to
enhance early diagnosis, enabling timely interventions to improve patient outcomes and quality of life, while
advancing cognitive health research.
